title: MORNING BID EUROPE-Feeding the AI beast
content: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Ankur Banerjee Investor angst over AI bellwethers' seemingly insatiable appetite for capital to build the infrastructure necessary for the technology to start paying off has cast a shadow over markets, as worries about valuations and fears over profitability persist. A series of reports from different corners of the globe has sharpened the focus on the AI trade this week, weighing on technology stocks. OpenAI has told investors its annualised revenue for September was almost $50 billion, a drop from what it signalled earlier, Reuters reported, while in Australia, data centre operator Firmus shelved its $5 billion initial public offering, and said it would opt for a private fundraising round instead. Over in the US, another massive round of fundraising appears to be on the way, with SpaceX, Broadcom and Oracle all expected to raise billions to buy high-end AI chips. Morgan Stanley estimates that AI infrastructure will require $1.5 trillion in external financing by 2028, with fundraising happening just as interest rates across the globe rise to combat the inflationary pressure from higher energy prices. That makes it more expensive to finance facilities whose returns may take years to materialise, while investors are also demanding greater visibility into the customers and cash flows that will support those investments. Meanwhile, public uneasiness with AI, and the small group of people who seemingly hold sway over it, has risen in recent months alongside concern that the technology could pose an existential threat to humanity. Brent crude futures remain above $100 per barrel with the war in the Middle East showing no signs of easing, with bond yields still at elevated levels. A months-long global bond selloff has pushed borrowing costs to multi-decade highs, with much of the pain being felt in France. The pressure built on the country on Thursday as euro zone finance ministers and the European Central Bank told France to pass a 2027 budget to calm bond markets. Key developments that could influence markets on Friday: European Central Bank's Piero Cipollone and Isabel Schnabel speak, Brazil inflation (September), Canada employment (September) (By Ankur Banerjee in Singapore; Editing by Kate Mayberry)

title: South Korea, Japan buffeted by hacks as AI lowers bar for cybercriminals
content: * TrendAI logged more cybersecurity incidents in Japan by September than during all of last year * Experts say AI erodes language and complexity barriers, enabling less-skilled hackers to find flaws * AI is making cybercrime faster, cheaper and harder to detect, experts say By Kyu-seok Shim, Brenda Goh and Kentaro Okasaka SEOUL/TOKYO, - South Korean and Japanese companies are racing to strengthen cyber defences after a wave of attacks that cybersecurity experts say are highlighting how AI may be lowering the bar for criminals with limited technical skills. Nine South Korean banks and two mega-churches are probing cyberattacks that may have involved AI tools, while Japanese companies including Daiwa Securities, SoftBank Corp and the Lawson convenience store chain have been hit by a recent surge in cyber incidents. Authorities are still investigating whether and how AI was used in many of the breaches. But cybersecurity specialists say the technology is helping attackers automate tasks from scanning for software vulnerabilities to crafting phishing campaigns, making cybercrime faster, cheaper and harder to detect. "AI doesn't get tired... My view is that Japan is essentially being subjected to carpet bombing," said Nobuo Miwa, president of Tokyo-based cybersecurity firm S&J Corp. Japan recorded more cybersecurity incidents in the first nine months of the year than in all of last year, according to data from TrendAI. Incidents rose to 86 in September, up about 18% from August and 37% from July. The rise suggests attackers have crossed a threshold in "effort, motivation and technical capability," while AI has largely erased language and other barriers that once hindered foreign hackers, Miwa said. US cybersecurity company CrowdStrike said a suspected 26-year-old China-based attacker behind the South Korean bank incidents would probably not have been able to carry out the campaign without AI assistance. The individual, whom CrowdStrike assessed was pursuing financial gain, used a Chinese-developed AI agent and Anthropic's Claude Code, according to the company. "While capabilities were not terribly sophisticated they were effective," said Adam Meyers, CrowdStrike's senior vice president of counter adversary operations. HARD-TO-DETECT ATTACKS AI-powered tools are also making it harder for defenders to spot suspicious behaviour, said Choi Kyoungjin, director of the Center for AI, Data and Policy at Gachon University near Seoul. "With general-purpose AI models, even ordinary users with malicious intent can ask the system to look for vulnerabilities and it will do much of that work for them," he said. South Korea reported 1,236 cyber incidents in the first half of the year, up 20% from a year earlier. While server hacking cases fell, reports of distributed denial-of-service attacks and ransomware rose 56.7% and 76.8% respectively, according to government data. The South Korean bank incidents underscored the need for stronger security controls and more rigorous testing as AI evolves, Meyers said. "The genie is out of the bottle, so to speak." Although the breaches have not yet resulted in material financial losses, risks could increase if stolen data is used in phishing or similar text-message "smishing" campaigns, Karen Wu, senior analyst at Fitch, wrote in a note. "We expect the incidents to result in regulatory penalties, customer compensation costs, and a sector-wide increase in cybersecurity spending," Wu said. DEFENCES NEED THEIR OWN BREAKTHROUGH Warnings about AI's growing role in cybercrime are increasingly coming from the technology's developers. Alphabet's Google and Anthropic have both warned that AI-assisted attacks are becoming more common globally. “At this point, we can assume that all threat actors are using AI in some capacity and their operations have benefited,” John Hultquist, the chief analyst at Google’s Threat Intelligence Group, said last month. Regulators in Japan and South Korea have begun responding. South Korea's Financial Services Commission has directed financial industry associations, regulators and affected executives to complete a 12-point cybersecurity self-assessment. In Japan, digital transformation minister Toshiharu Furukawa convened a meeting of ministries and agencies on Thursday following the recent attacks. The National Cybersecurity Office plans to issue warnings to businesses. S&J's Miwa said he expected elevated levels of cyberattacks to persist. "The attackers have experienced a breakthrough that has rendered many of the old assumptions obsolete," he said. "Our defences need their own breakthrough as well." title: Chinese developer makes ARTEX AI agent closed-source after Korean bank hack
content: By Brenda Goh SEOUL, - The Chinese developer of ARTEX said they have converted the AI agent to a closed-source project after cybersecurity firms identified it as a tool used in a recent cyberattack campaign against South Korean banks. "Given the misuse of the tool, the ARTEX project will no longer be updated and will be converted to closed source. No further versions will be released to the public nor will maintenance support be provided," the developer, who uses the GitHub handle "Autumn-27", said on the code-hosting platform on Thursday. They said the original aim of ARTEX was to help enterprises and organizations conduct security risk testing and improve their security capabilities. Without explicitly addressing the South Korean bank attacks, they said they opposed any illegal use of the software and bore no responsibility for conduct that violates laws and regulations. ARTEX's Github page has been taken down, according to Reuters' checks. US cybersecurity firm Crowdstrike said on Wednesday the suspect behind recent cyberattacks at South Korean banks aimed at stealing customers' personal data was likely a ​China-based 26-year-old who used the ARTEX AI agent and Anthropic's Claude Code. Released on GitHub this year, ARTEX is an open-source AI agent designed to automate penetration testing. It is not a standalone large language model but ⁠connects to ​external LLMs such as ChatGPT, Claude and DeepSeek to help organisations test for vulnerabilities in their ​networks. At least nine South Korean banks have disclosed or been reported by local media as targets of cyberattacks since late September, prompting police to launch ​a probe this week and President Lee Jae Myung to call for robust response measures. Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told a regular press briefing on Thursday that the ministry was not familiar with the ​case, adding that China consistently opposes and combats hacking activities. title: Jio’s 1,600-satellite LEO network: 23 ground stations, remote area coverage and more
content: Reliance Jio has showcased its proposed 1,600-satellite Low Earth Orbit (LEO) network at the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 in New Delhi on Thursday, October 8. There are 23 ground stations in the plan to ensure connectivity in remote villages, islands, and border areas where conventional mobile towers and fibre networks are difficult to deploy, according to Jio’s presentation at India Mobile Congress 2026. The project was unveiled by Jio with its vision, ‘Sovereign Satellite Connectivity'. The network, the company claimed, would be able to cover land and sea areas, as well as areas with more than 600,000 villages. The system will also be integrated with Jio's terrestrial network, establishing a hybrid satellite-to-ground communications network. Jio plans 1,600 LEO satellites and 23 ground stations Jio shared its plans for the constellation during the IMC 2026 presentation, which include about 1,600 LEO satellites and 23 ground stations. These stations would be used to link the satellite network to ground-based infrastructure. Jio stated that the entire value chain should be in India. This includes design, engineering, integration, testing, launch, deployment and operations of a satellite. The firm also has direct-to-device calling in rural areas. Other potential applications can include enterprise connectivity, remote locations, aviation, maritime, government, defence and disaster response. Also Read | Jio users get free Canva Pro for 1 year: Check eligible plans and how to claim Jio targets remote villages, islands and border areas Jio’s display outlines a goal of 100% coverage across land and maritime areas. The company mentioned remote villages, islands and border outposts with low levels of conventional connectivity. The satellite network will not replace Jio's existing terrestrial network, but will be an addition to it. This might enable users to remain connected where fibre rollout and mobile towers are not viable. The 1,600-satellite network is still a proposal Jio explained that the 1,600 satellites and 23 ground stations are under a proposed plan. India's space regulatory body, IN-SPACe, recently, in July 2026, reviewed the proposed constellation, which was found to be technically viable and similar to satellite connectivity systems worldwide. Jio has also approached the government for permission to file applications with the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and synced its orbits with other satellite service providers. There have been reports of a phased development schedule, with a test flight in September 2027, 400-450 satellites planned for completion by 2030, and the full constellation by 2035. But Jio didn't reveal any launch timeline for the constellation at IMC 26. Also Read | Jio Platforms aspires to deliver India’s biggest IPO, says Akash Ambani Satellite network aligns with IMC 2026 theme The Prime Minister, Narendra Modi, inaugurated the 10th India Mobile Congress on Thursday, October 8, with the theme ‘Scale Without Boundaries'. Jio called its satellite connectivity vision “reflects” this theme, as it aims to provide network access where traditional telecom infrastructure cannot be deployed due to geographical or deployment constraints.

title: Temple is unlike any smartwatch: Why Deepinder Goyal’s ₹1 lakh Brain Flow tech wearable is sparking buzz
content: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal’s new Temple wearable is drawing attention for a simple reason: it does not sit on your wrist. The device is small and pill-shaped and is attached to the side of the head to monitor aspects of the brain's blood flow. Goyal has said that the applications of Temple could extend beyond fitness tracking, including checking whether pilots are fit to fly. Goyal posted the comments on X on Thursday, October 8, following his announcement that pre-orders in India would open soon. He said that he “certainly would have it on pilots” and noted that perhaps the Indian Air Force can use it to determine who is the fittest for a given mission. However, Temple is not approved, established and certified as a pilot-fitness or aviation safety device at this time. Temple is not your usual smartwatch Temple is designed to fit between the forehead and the ear. It is not like wearing a watch strap; it is secured by disposable adhesive ‘Grips’. According to Goyal and Temple, the device can remain on during activities such as running, swimming and showering. The company states the grips will last up to seven days, but recommends changing them every two to three days, especially when sweating or exposed to dust. The launch version is expected in six colours: True Gold, Rose Gold, Black Mirror, Real Jade, Deep Blue and Purple Funk. Also Read | Google launches Playground to create video games with AI, partners with WIF BrainFlow: The technology behind Temple Temple employs photoplethysmography (PPG), a technology that's also used in smartwatches. But instead of measuring signals from the wrist, Temple places the sensor near the temple. The company calls this system BrainFlow. It is used to monitor the changes in cerebral blood flow. Goyal said the data could eventually be used to provide insights into sleep, recovery, exercise and stress response. BrainFlow does not measure brain activity directly like an EEG, however, and Temple is not able to diagnose medical conditions at this time. What do the studies show? Goyal has published two validation studies. The first had 23 healthy adults who were compared against BrainFlow readings while pedalling and changing posture with Transcranial Doppler measurements. A second study looked at 44 healthy men who participated in 60 sessions. According to results shared by Goyal , BrainFlow showed correlations of up to 0.91 with changes in brain blood volume measured using time-domain near-infrared spectroscopy. Both studies are preprints and have yet to be peer-reviewed. Thus, the results have to be validated independently. Also Read | CMF Watch 3 Pro review: Can its heart rate tracking keep up with daily fitness? Why pilots and air force Goyal's comments are indicative of a potential capability, not an existing one. It is theoretically possible that continuous physiological data could be used to assess a person's condition prior to a high-stakes task. For the time being, there is no evidence that Temple can make a determination on whether a commercial pilot is medically fit to fly. There are still existing medical and regulatory procedures that govern aviation fitness decisions. Temple could cost around ₹ 1 lakh Earlier, Goyal had said that the cost of a Temple in India is around ₹ 1 lakh. The final India price is not yet available. Pre-orders should be available soon, and waitlist users will receive priority . The company is also testing ideas for thought-to-text technology, though he anticipates that it will be several years in the future. For now, the fact that Temple is positioned so uniquely, has BrainFlow technology and has such ambitious future applications, separates it from standard smartwatches and fitness trackers.

title: ‘Cyber fraud does not respect borders’: PM Modi seeks global mechanism at IMC 2026
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday called for a global mechanism to tackle cross-border cyber fraud and the growing threat of deepfakes. PM Modi appealed to governments, technology providers, telecom operators and financial institutions to collaborate to prevent digital fraud reaching users at the 10th India Mobile Congress (IMC) in New Delhi on October 8, 2026. Modi stated that cybercrime is not confined to national boundaries and that the scalability of digital technology requires users to trust it. The Indian nation has also accumulated extensive experience in dealing with cyber fraud and is poised to share it with other nations, he added. Modi urges global action against cyber fraud "Technology achieves scale only when it gains trust," Modi said, according to the Press Information Bureau (PIB) transcript of his October 8 address. He noted that a criminal from one country may target a victim in another country with the assistance of a third country. Coordinated international action has become even more crucial with the introduction of deepfakes that add another layer to the challenge. Modi urged the GSMA and telecoms companies across the globe to help develop a mechanism which can detect and prevent fraud before it reaches customers. Also Read | Google launches Playground to create video games with AI, partners with WIF Phone and data security need stronger safeguards The Prime Minister stated that growth in telecommunications should go hand in hand with enhanced security. For regular users, digital trust means knowing who is calling, verifying it's a real message, and ensuring payments are safe and personal information is protected, he said. "Cyber fraud and cyber crimes do not respect borders," Modi said, stressing that governments, technology companies, telecom operators and financial institutions must work together. These comments follow the adoption of smartphones and internet services as the mainstay of digital payments, education, healthcare and government services in India. Modi highlights ₹ 50 lakh crore DBT transfers Modi also talked about the digital governance framework and mobile-linked banking for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) in India. According to the PIB, Modi said nearly ₹ 50 lakh crore had been transferred directly to beneficiaries through the system. He said that the loss of ₹ 5 lakh crore was averted from ‘wrong hands’ due to leakages. The government continued to work hard to curb such wastage and ensure public money reached the target users, Modi said. Also Read | Boston Dynamics appoints former Amazon executive Rohit Prasad as CEO India moving from technology consumer to creator It was also a platform which Modi had used to highlight India's evolving role in the global technology landscape. The nation has shifted from a technology consumption mode to a creation mode and has begun focusing on Indian designs, technology, and IP, he added. He added that the 10th edition of IMC will help chart the course of the next decade in the mobile industry, both in India and across the globe.

title: Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra pre-orders open: Price, specs, 128GB RAM and sale date
content: Microsoft has announced pre-orders for the new 15-inch Surface laptop with Nvidia's RTX Spark platform. The company unveiled the device at its Windows and Surface event in San Francisco on October 7 2026, as a high-performance device for AI workloads that developers, creators, and users can run locally. The Surface Laptop Ultra costs $2,599 (approx. ₹ 2.3 lakh) and will be available for sale from October 16. Microsoft claims that the laptop's unified memory can be expanded to 128GB and used to run large AI models without relying on cloud services. The company also unveiled the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box for developers. Surface Laptop Ultra price and specifications The Surface Laptop Ultra uses Nvidia's RTX Spark Superchip, which consists of the Blackwell RTX GPU and up to 6,144 GPU cores, plus Nvidia's Grace CPU with up to 20 cores and up to 128GB of unified memory, according to Microsoft. The entry model costs $2,599 and includes an 18-core CPU, a 5,120-core GPU, 24GB of RAM, and a 512GB SSD. The 32GB RAM and 1TB storage option is available for $3,299. The higher-end 20-core CPU configuration starts at $3,599 with 32 GB RAM. Prices rise to $3,999 for 48GB, $4,299 for 64GB and $5,899 for 128GB RAM. CNET reported on October 7 that the 128GB version was already listed as out of stock. Also Read | Apple Mac Studio M5 Ultra turns desktop into high-powered AI workstation Built for local AI and demanding workloads Microsoft claims the laptop can deliver up to 1 petaflop of AI performance and run AI models with more than 120 billion parameters locally. The company will focus on developers, creators and professionals who want more computing power but don't want to push all workloads to the cloud. The 15-inch PixelSense Ultra display is said to be the brightest Microsoft has ever made for a laptop, and the laptop will also feature a 30% bigger haptic touchpad. It's less than 18 mm thick and weighs less than 4.5 lbs. Magnetic USB-C charging and more ports There are some interesting hardware changes as well, with Magnetic Connect, a magnetic charging interface for USB-C devices, being one of the highlights. The charging port can still be used for data and video. There are also two extra USB-C connectors, HDMI, USB-A, SD card readers and 3.5mm headphone jacks. Microsoft claims it can connect up to three external 4K screens. Also Read | Apple Mac mini with M5 or M6 chip may debut before iPhone 18 Pro event Microsoft expands local AI push Local AI was a big theme of the event. Microsoft has revealed the availability of MAI Code 1.1 flash, DeepSeek V4 flash and Nvidia Nemotron models on Windows for local use. Microsoft also announced that its AI agent, Meta Muse, will be made into a standalone Windows application. The company emphasised Microsoft Execution Containers, intended to isolate AI agents while enabling them to carry out tasks. Surface RTX Spark Dev Box also launched In addition to the laptop, Microsoft announced it will open pre-orders for the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, targeted at AI engineers and developers. It begins at $5,999 and supports up to 128GB and up to 1 petalops of AI performance. In addition, Microsoft is providing up to $1,000 in cash back to customers who trade in an eligible MacBook Pro, an effort to attract professional users to the new Surface Laptop Ultra.

title: One Tech Tip: Lake America backlash fuels interest in Google Maps alternatives
content: Just because Google and Apple are now calling it Lake America doesn't mean everyone has to. After President Donald Trump ordered a new name for Lake Ontario, the two U.S. tech giants quickly fell in line, relabeling the body of water on their digital maps . The move sparked a backlash among some users, already unhappy with the companies' decisions to rename the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America on their maps following a previous Trump edict. The controversy and lingering worries about digital privacy have fueled interest in map services that aren't from Big Tech companies, especially Google Maps, which is the dominant player with about 80% of the market, according to most estimates. Here’s a rundown of some of the most popular free map app alternatives: MapQuest has been around for three decades but was overtaken by the rise of Google. It's now owned by California company System1. Downloads of the MapQuest app surged in early September after Apple renamed Lake Ontario, topping the free app charts in both the U.S. and Canada on Apple's App Store. The MapQuest app has real time traffic updates and turn by turn route guidance, and shows what's nearby, like gas stations and coffee shops. However, the app isn't available outside the U.S. and Canada. But people in other countries can still use the MapQuest website. The company is currently looking into making MapQuest more broadly accessible, after receiving requests for the app from “people in multiple countries," spokesperson Anne Brownlee said. Another granddaddy in the mapping world, TomTom helped popularize GPS route mapping with the 2004 release of its TomTom GO, which the Dutch company says was the world’s first all-in-one portable satellite navigation device. TomTom still sells physical devices but it also has a free map app for Google and Android phones that is designed “exclusively for drivers” with live traffic data and info on road hazards. The TomTom app's mobile interface is clean and basic, with no ads and few extra features or settings. But its focus on drivers means there are no other route options such as walking or cycling. HERE WeGo has been hailed by some as the closest non-Big Tech alternative to Google Maps. It began life as Nokia Maps and is now owned by a consortium of German carmakers including Audi, BMW, and Mercedes-Benz. The free app, available for both iOS and Android devices, offers many of the same features as Google Maps. There's route mapping for various modes of transport — car, public transport, walking, bike and, in some regions, taxi. Like Google Maps, drivers can add multiple stops to routes and users can choose different maps views like terrain, traffic and satellite — but there's no Street View. If mobile signal is spotty or nonexistent, users can download country maps to navigate offline. Offline maps can also be downloaded on Google Maps, but the area is limited and they expire after a year. HERE WeGo is just one of many lesser-known map apps based in the European Union that embrace the bloc’s strict privacy framework known as GDPR. Unlike Google, they don’t rely on vacuuming up masses of user data to sell ads targeted at those users. HERE WeGo's business model is based on licensing deals with businesses like trucking companies. Others sell premium subscriptions alongside free versions. Estonia's Organic Maps is completely free and based on data from the volunteer-run OpenStreetMap database. Netherlands-based OSMand is similar, but a subscription is needed for more than just basic functions. Magic Earth is a Dutch route planner that says it never collects personal data or tracks user movements. Sygic, from Slovakia, is a GPS route navigation app that offers free offline maps, but you’ll have to buy a subscription to get extra features including traffic updates, speed camera warnings and a dashcam function. Mapy.com, from a Czech technology company, is an outdoor route planner known for detailed hiking and trail maps that can be downloaded for use offline. Need to get across town without a car? Citymapper is a free journey planning app that’s a major rival to Google Maps when it comes to finding the best routes around a city on public transportation. The app covers 430 cities around the world and options include bus, subway and ferry routes as well as taxi, rental bike and scooter options. This GPS navigation map is focused on providing route guidance for drivers. It’s known for crowdsourcing real time traffic information such as car accidents and police speed cameras from other drivers. But don’t be fooled by the name. Although it has its own distinct app and branding, Waze is actually owned by Google, which bought it in 2013. ___ Is there a tech topic that you think needs explaining? title: Samsung flags $80 billion profit on AI boom, highest quarterly for any tech company
content: By Heekyong Yang and Hyunjoo Jin SEOUL, Oct 8 (Reuters) - Samsung Electronics on Thursday projected its quarterly profit would top 100 trillion won, a world first for a technology company, estimating a nearly nine-fold jump in third-quarter earnings as booming demand for AI chips drove strong memory sales. The world's largest memory chipmaker estimated an operating profit of 107.4 trillion won ($80.17 billion) for the July-September period, slightly ahead of an LSEG SmartEstimate of 106.1 trillion won. The forecast marks Samsung's fourth straight quarter of record operating profit, underscoring a deepening global memory chip shortage as AI infrastructure investment outpaces supply growth, which has driven chip prices up sharply. Samsung and Micron expect the imbalance to persist into 2028, although Chinese competition and a potential slowdown in AI spending pose risks to the longer-term earnings outlook. Samsung's shares moved sideways despite flagging another record profit, slipping 0.2% in early trade versus a 0.5% fall in the benchmark KOSPI. Its share price has slumped more than 25% from a record high in June amid concerns about the durability of the AI boom. Analysts have also recently trimmed their forecasts due to the sharp appreciation of the South Korean currency, which reduces the value of dollar-denominated overseas sales when converted into local currency. "The market's focus has shifted to whether the sharp earnings growth that started a year ago would be sustainable," market analyst Kim Seok-hwan at Mirae Asset Securities said. Analysts expect profit in the fourth quarter to grow 8.2% from the previous quarter, slowing from 20% sequential quarterly growth in the third quarter, with chip price growth abating. Market research firm TrendForce expects conventional DRAM contract prices to rise 10% to 15% in the fourth quarter from the preceding quarter, much slower than a second-quarter surge of ​roughly 60%. The moderation in memory prices is being closely watched by investors after a more than year-long rally that propelled profit margins to record highs for the world's largest memory producers Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron. Third-quarter revenue would likely rise 127% to 195 trillion won from a year earlier, Samsung said. The company will release detailed results, including a breakdown of earnings by business division, on October 29. BIGGER-THAN-EXPECTED MOBILE LOSS Memory chips are expected to account for the bulk of the earnings improvement. Prices have soared due to the tight supply of conventional DRAM and NAND chips as well as growing demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM), essential for processing vast amounts of data for AI applications. Douglas Kim of Douglas Research Advisory estimated that Samsung's HBM bit shipments expanded by close to 50% quarter-over-quarter in the third quarter, with Samsung trying to narrow the gap with SK Hynix in the HBM market. But the memory chip boom presents a challenge for Samsung's other businesses, particularly its smartphone and consumer electronics divisions, which face mounting pressure from higher component costs. Samsung's mobile business posted a larger-than-expected loss of more than $1 billion in the third quarter, analysts said. Meanwhile, Samsung's contract chipmaking, or foundry, business is expected to remain loss-making because of the burden of fixed costs and still-low utilisation rates, analysts said. However, utilisation is expected to improve over the next several quarters, supported by stronger demand for advanced manufacturing processes. Samsung has been seeking to narrow the gap with industry leader TSMC in advanced contract chip manufacturing. Investors said they would also be closely watching for details of Samsung's shareholder return policy during its earnings call later this month. title: Smart glasses privacy concerns grow: Norway, Australia, UK and US curb Meta Ray-Ban use
content: Smart glasses are moving from a futuristic gadget to a growing privacy concern as governments, courts, regulators, and businesses rethink where camera-equipped wearables are allowed. The most prominent feature is Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses, which can capture photos, videos and audio and use AI capabilities, yet appear to be just regular glasses. The concern is that people nearby may not know when they are being recorded. The debate has intensified after Norway proposed a temporary ban on AI glasses in certain public areas. Australia is looking at limitations in the government sector, and courts in the UK and the US have already done so in their jurisdictions. Recent cases in France and the Dutch firms have placed pressure on Meta and other smart glasses makers, Reuters reported. Norway moves towards a temporary ban Norway is making the strongest regulatory move. The Norwegian government, on 5 October, announced its intention to propose a temporary ban on AI glasses in specific public locations, such as parks, beaches, museums, shopping centres and public events. Schools, childcare centres, health care facilities, gyms and places with changing rooms could also be included in the proposal. Torgeir Micaelsen, Minister of Digitalisation and Public Governance of Norway, expressed concern that some people might be photographed, filmed or recorded without their awareness. Norway also intends to establish an expert group to recommend lasting rules. Also Read | How HRMS cuts management costs by 90% and AI helps routine queries by up to 80% Australia explores work restrictions Australia is also reviewing the technology. The federal government in September announced it was considering limiting the use of smart glasses with cameras in government workplaces due to privacy and security concerns, Reuters reported. The move comes as Australian authorities separately work on broader privacy reforms covering emerging technologies. On 31 August, Attorney-General Michelle Rowland announced that one of the technologies of concern was smart glasses that used AI as more people gain access to such devices. UK and US courts restrict smart glasses In the UK, courts have banned the use of Meta smart glasses due to existing restrictions on recordings in court. On 20 August, the UK Cinema Association also announced that some cinema operators were rolling out measures to limit or ban the use of camera-enabled smart glasses due to privacy and film piracy concerns, Reuters reported. Starting 20 July, the Unified Court System in New York, USA, banned smart glasses in courthouses. The rule applies to all eyewear that has a camera, microphone or other technology that can record audio or video. Also Read | Should AI agents have the power to act without asking us first? Privacy backlash spreads across Europe The problem is also spreading to France and the Netherlands. The investigations by Paris prosecutors were initiated in September after complaints of women being filmed without their consent through connected glasses. Meanwhile, Dutch retailer Hans Anders suspended sales of Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses in the Netherlands and Belgium on 2 October, citing growing public and political concerns. Meta claims that the glasses include an LED light to indicate when they're recording and anti-tampering features. However, regulators and governments are increasingly wondering if that protection is sufficient. The larger issue for the industry is now whether smart glasses can record people. The question is whether society is comfortable with always-available cameras on people's faces in everyday public spaces, according to the Reuters report.

title: McDonalds sued over AI tool that recommends prices to US franchisees
content: McDonald’s is facing a federal lawsuit that alleges its AI-enhanced pricing tool violates antitrust laws because it shares nonpublic data with franchisees who might be competing in the same market. The lawsuit, which was filed Friday in Illinois, said McDonald’s pricing tool uses artificial intelligence to collect data that competing franchises wouldn’t normally share, like store-level sales. The Chicago-based burger giant has said it makes the tool available to U.S. franchisees to help them set prices at their individual restaurants. The lawsuit also blames the pricing system for raising McDonald’s U.S. prices. “McDonald’s has built and for years deployed its own information-sharing pricing platform, which draws on data from its millions of daily transactions to set menu prices across thousands of U.S. restaurants,” the lawsuit states. “The result is algorithmic price-fixing aimed at customers who are already stretched thin.” McDonald’s said Tuesday that the lawsuit is “filled with inaccuracies” and it would vigorously defend itself. “AI does not set menu prices at McDonald’s restaurants – McDonald’s franchisees do,” the company said in a statement. “Optional tools are available to franchisees to help them make the best decisions for their businesses and customers, but these tools do not automate, coordinate or fix pricing in any way.” The lawsuit was filed on behalf of a consumer, Michael Thomas, of DeKalb, Illinois. According to the lawsuit, Thomas frequently visits McDonald’s and orders a Quarter Pounder with cheese, french fries and a Coke. The lawsuit said Thomas noticed price differences between McDonald’s stores near his home. McDonald's said it has used an AI-enhanced pricing tool for more than a decade. The program determines the optimal price for menu items based on a store’s sales, location and other factors, including competitors’ prices. McDonald's said that long before adopting the AI-enhanced tool, it collected data and recommended prices to its franchisees, who own and operate 95% of McDonald’s 14,000 U.S. stores. “All we do is provide the context of what’s going on,” a McDonald’s spokesman told The Associated Press. “We don’t have any way to affect the menu pricing in a restaurant.” But the lawsuit said McDonald's has “significant leverage over its franchisees” and can pressure them to follow its pricing recommendations. The Associated Press left a message Tuesday with the National Owners Association, which represents McDonald’s franchisees. McDonald’s has been experimenting with various value strategies in the U.S. and other markets for several years as it tries to win back lower-income consumers, whose visits to fast-food chains have dropped. But franchisees don’t always follow its guidance. During a conference call with investors in August, McDonald’s Chairman and CEO Chris Kempczinski said only 60% of its U.S. restaurants were offering McDonald’s proposed menu of 10 items for under $3. “As you know, in our system, that’s not something that we just flip the switch on,” Kempczinski said. “It requires conversations with franchisees.” The lawsuit asks the judge to certify the case as a class action and to require McDonald's to pay damages to the class. It also seeks to prevent McDonald's from enforcing agreements that restrict competition. This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: World Bank says India should scale small AI applications instead of betting heavily on frontier models
content: New Delhi [India], October 6 (ANI): India should focus on expanding the use of existing artificial intelligence applications across the economy and selectively invest in frontier AI capabilities instead of making broad investments in developing advanced models from scratch, Vincent Belinga, Senior Economist at the World Bank, told ANI in an exclusive conversation. Belinga said India should follow a three-stage approach to AI development: adoption, adaptation and frontier development. "One is adoption, meaning using existing application. The second is adaptation, meaning taking open source AI and adapting them to local conditions. And then the third stage is frontier model, meaning developing the next capability from scratch," Belinga said. He said India's immediate priority should be to deepen AI adoption among firms and workers, as adoption is increasing but remains limited across the economy. "What we recommend for India is doing the two. Meaning, deepening adoption so that many firms, millions of firms, millions of workers use AI more productively because so far we see that adoption is increasing but not broad based," he said. Belinga said India already has promising AI applications in areas such as education and healthcare, but many of these initiatives are either limited to specific states or remain at the project stage. The focus, he said, should be on taking such applications to a larger population. "Some promising small AI in education, in health that are either state specific or that are still at project level. So, what we need is to scale up these initiatives so that they are broadly shared across all the states or enriching the broader population," he said. The World Bank report highlights local AI applications in India, including Bhashini and AI4Bharat for multilingual access to services, DIKSHA for personalised learning, KATHIR and the PM-KISAN chatbot for agriculture, and AI-assisted tuberculosis screening from chest X-rays. Belinga said broad-based deployment across sectors would be more important for India than relying on productivity gains from only a few industries. "AI is going to raise productivity," he said, adding that India needs to ensure that AI is adopted across sectors and by workers. The World Bank estimates that 14 per cent of Indian workers are in jobs where AI can complement their work and raise productivity. It also estimates that AI could add 0.1-0.8 percentage points to annual labour productivity growth over the next decade, depending on the pace of AI deployment and complementary investments. Belinga said India should also be selective in developing frontier AI capabilities because such development requires significant resources. "Frontier development is very resourceful. I mean, you see what happening in the US, you have billions of dollar to be invested in frontier development. And given that India has competing development needs, what we suggest is to invest selectively in frontier capabilities where India has a comparative advantage," he said. He said the broader objective should be to deploy smaller AI applications across sectors such as education, healthcare, agriculture, finance and IT so that productivity gains are spread across the economy rather than concentrated in individual sectors. "So you have to make sure that broadly, AI is being adopted and you deploy these small applications across all the economy so that we can have larger productivity gain instead of having productivity gain at sectoral level," Belinga said. (ANI)

title: India among top 10 emerging markets in AI readiness; private AI investment triples: World Bank
content: New Delhi, Oct 6 (PTI) India is among the top 10 leading emerging-market performers in artificial intelligence (AI) readiness and is well positioned to harness the technology, helped by its large technical workforce, globally integrated IT sector and digital public infrastructure, the World Bank said on Tuesday. In its latest report titled 'India and Artificial Intelligence: Seizing the Development Opportunity', the World Bank said private investment in AI in India more than tripled to USD 4.1 billion in 2025 from USD 1.2 billion in 2024. At the same time, the number of professionals employed by Global Capability Centres (GCCs) rose to 2.36 million in 2025 from 1.9 million a year ago, it said. The report, however, noted that the long-term economic and labour market impact of AI remains uncertain. It called for cross-cutting policy measures to deepen AI-enabling infrastructure, improve the business environment, broaden access to AI and enhance labour capacity so that the benefits of the technology are widely shared. "India is one of the top 10 leading emerging-market performers on AI readiness," said Paul Procee, World Bank Acting Country Director for India. "Harnessing AI as a development tool – not just a technology – could be one of the most powerful levers India has to boost productivity and improve public services," he said. The World Bank Group is also investing through AgriConnect in 'small AI' targeted and locally adapted tools aimed at ensuring that the benefits of AI reach a wider section of the population while supporting workers through the transition, he said. The India Development Update is a companion to the World Bank Group's South Asia Economic Update, which examines economic developments and prospects in the region. The latest South Asia Economic Update projects that South Asia will grow 6.9 per cent in 2026, retaining its position as the world's fastest-growing region, the report said. For most of South Asia, the biggest gains from AI are likely to come from adopting and adapting the technology to local conditions, including through small AI applications suited to low-resource settings, it said. The report said complementary measures would also be needed to reduce barriers to AI adoption by small firms, promote local AI innovation and establish a clear regulatory framework that reduces uncertainty while safeguarding data security and privacy. "The adoption of AI has the potential to transform South Asia's development trajectory by boosting labour productivity, expanding export opportunities, and improving public service delivery," said Franziska Ohnsorge, World Bank Group Chief Economist for Asia. "But to reap these benefits, governments need to address the foundational gaps that hold back adoption," she said. The Update recommended strengthening workforce skills, creating a more business-enabling environment and improving physical as well as digital infrastructure.

title: UK watchdog opens first Online Safety Act probe into Meta
content: By Paul Sandle LONDON, Oct 6 (Reuters) - Britain's communications regulator opened its first formal investigation into Meta under the Online Safety Act on Tuesday, questioning whether it properly assessed risks posed by its Instagram Instants feature before launching it in May. Instants allows content shared by users on Instagram to disappear after being viewed. Ofcom said its investigation would establish whether Meta carried out a "suitable and sufficient" assessment of the risks of illegal content on the feature and any risks posed to children before its launch. George Lusty, director of enforcement at Ofcom, said: "Our online safety laws are clear — significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched." Safety by design had to be built in and not bolted on, he said. "Today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," he said. Meta said it took its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously. "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," a spokesperson said. "Instants has in-built protections, including blocking screenshots, reshares and forwarding, no public feed, and Teen Account protections on automatically." "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation," the spokesperson said. Ofcom's first investigation under the Online Safety Act was into an online suicide discussion forum last year, followed by probes into pornography sites, file-sharing services used to distribute child sexual abuse material, and platforms such as 4chan. Britain's online safety regime sets obligations for social media platforms, search engines and adult content providers to tackle illegal content and to protect children's safety. Ofcom requires companies to conduct risk assessments and implement safety measures, such as age verification. If a company fails to comply, Ofcom can impose fines of up to £18 million or 10% of qualifying worldwide revenue, whichever is greater. Meta has launched legal challenges against Ofcom over its implementation of the act, including the scale and scope of information it has to provide to the regulator and the level of fees Ofcom charges. In January, Ofcom launched an investigation into Meta over the provision of information about its WhatsApp Business product under a separate Communications Act. (Reporting by Raechel Thankam Job in Bengaluru and Paul Sandle in London; Editing by Mrigank Dhaniwala, Sarah Young and Tomasz Janowski)

title: Is era of affordable smartphones ending? HMD India CEO warns prices may stay high till 2027
content: The era of ultra-affordable smartphones could be coming under pressure as rising costs of memory and other components push device prices higher, said Ravi Kunwar, VP & CEO, HMD India-APAC, in an exclusive interview with LiveMint during the HMD Vibe 2 Pro 5G launch in India. He added that cost pressures may persist in the industry until the end of 2027. Kunwar said that HMD is focusing on features that will be useful in practice, battery life, and those specifically helpful in the Indian market, rather than going into an aggressive price war. The company has officially introduced the Vibe 2 Pro 5G at discounted prices, starting from ₹ 14,999 for the 6GB RAM configuration and ₹ 16,999 for the 8GB RAM configuration, and it will be available for sale from 8 October during Flipkart's Big Billion Days sale. Rising component costs could keep phones expensive In the interview, Kunwar said smartphone component prices have risen considerably over the last six months, especially those of memory prices. Growing demand for memory due to artificial intelligence (AI) is part of that pressure, he said. Manufacturers will continue to seek to optimize their supply chains and costs, but that pressure is not expected to last long, Kunwar said. “The challenge is going to remain till probably the good end of 2027,” he added. As the high input costs become universal, “consumers will have to get used to the higher prices of smartphones,” he shared. Also Read | HMD Vibe2 Pro 5G launched: First impressions of the new smartphone HMD targets value-conscious buyers The pressure might be greater in the sub- ₹ 20,000 smartphone price band, which accounts for about 40% of the Indian smartphone market, Kunwar said. He added that consumers facing higher prices could delay upgrades. With this, HMD is shifting the Vibe 2 Pro 5G's focus toward features targeted at heavy users. The smartphone gets a 6,000mAh battery, 33W fast charging, dual speakers, dual microphones and a MediaTek Dimensity 6300 processor. It also comes with a 120Hz display. Kunwar said the upgrades were driven by customer feedback following the Vibe 2 5G, which continues to have a 4.5-star rating on Flipkart, according to HMD. Sarvam AI brings local language focus HMD also hopes AI will help it differentiate its phones in India. Vibe 2 Pro 5G has been enhanced with Sarvam AI, which will support 22 Indian languages and take into account regional and cultural contexts. Kunwar said the goal is to make AI a regular part of consumers' lives, particularly beyond India's major metropolitan areas. Also Read | Vivo V80 India launch date, camera, battery and display details confirmed HMD plans to expand beyond entry-level phones Kunwar said that HMD is not planning to stick with the affordable smart devices. The company is slowly climbing the price ladder, having introduced its products at ₹ 10,000 and later in the ₹ 14,000- ₹ 17,000 range. Eventually, he said, the company wants to be a full-line player in each smartphone price segment. “Our motto is not about being the loudest in the marketplace; it is about being the most trusted,” Kunwar said.

title: South Koreas Lee says AI appears to have been used in bank hacks
content: SEOUL, - South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Tuesday that AI models are believed to have been used in some recent hacking incidents against banks and called for the country to develop cybersecurity methods suited to the AI era. • "In some hacking incidents, signs have emerged of AI being used, causing considerable public concern and anxiety," Lee said during a cabinet meeting. "Please establish the circumstances swiftly and clearly, and concentrate personnel and resources on minimising the damage." • South Korea's police have launched a full-scale investigation into the hacking attacks against commercial banks that led to a breach of customers' personal information, the Yonhap news agency reported on Tuesday. • Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and others had reported cyberattacks, the Financial Services Commission said on Friday, while Yonhap reported that Hana Bank and Woori Bank had also suffered breaches. • Authorities have not yet disclosed details on what kind of AI tools were used in the hacking incidents or the full scale of the breaches. • On Sunday, FSC Chairman Lee Eog-weon convened an emergency meeting with financial industry associations, regulators and executives from affected institutions, warning that the sector must respond with the highest level of vigilance. • In September, Australia said an OpenAI agent breached a government health data portal in June, gaining unauthorised access to files, in what could be the ‌first known instance of an AI agent hacking a government website. • An artificial intelligence research firm said last week that AI agents tried to hack into a Canadian government website, casting the effort as a failed hacking attempt, while Canada said there were ​no indications its systems were compromised. title: UP govt aims to establish Lucknow among Indias leading AI innovation cities: Yogi Adityanath
content: Lucknow, Oct 6 (PTI) Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday said the state government aims to establish Lucknow among India's leading AI innovation cities and will support at least 50 AI-focussed startups in the city over the next five years. Addressing an event marking the 10th anniversary of HCLTech's Lucknow campus, Adityanath called on the IT major to partner with the government in developing a strong AI innovation ecosystem in the state capital. The chief minister said the government would provide full support to establish, strengthen and help the startups access global markets. "We have to make Lucknow not just a centre for IT services but a major hub for AI, semiconductors, cyber security, computing technology and deep tech," he said, stressing the need for the government and industry to work together. Adityanath said HCL's journey in Lucknow was a matter of pride for Uttar Pradesh, noting that founder Shiv Nadar had started his journey from the state nearly five decades ago. "HCL chose Lucknow and Lucknow adopted HCL," he said, adding that the company's campus, established 10 years ago, had given a new dimension to the partnership. He said the success of the campus was not merely about business or employment, but was also linked to the aspirations of families whose children had found career opportunities in the city. Referring to the state's workforce, Adityanath said Uttar Pradesh's young and talented population was its biggest strength. "Today, I proudly say that I have India's youngest workforce, and its talent is my greatest strength," he said. Adityanath further said that a decade ago, young people from Uttar Pradesh often had to move to Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad for better career opportunities, but the situation had changed and young people were now choosing Lucknow for their careers. The chief minister said Uttar Pradesh's infrastructure and connectivity had also expanded significantly. The roughly 1,200-km journey from Ballia to Bijnor could now be completed in about 10 hours, compared with several days a decade ago, he said. On the state's IT and electronics sector, Adityanath claimed Uttar Pradesh accounted for around 55 per cent of India's mobile manufacturing and nearly 60 per cent of the electronic components manufactured in the country. He said the state's IT and IT-enabled services exports, which stood at around ₹ 12,000-15,000 crore a decade ago, had crossed ₹ 1 lakh crore and the government was targeting ₹ 2.5 lakh crore over the next four years. Electronics exports have also risen from around ₹ 3,800 crore a decade ago to ₹ 45,000 crore, with a target of ₹ 2 lakh crore by 2030, he said. Adityanath said the IT sector was no longer limited to Noida, with IT parks operating in Lucknow, Kanpur, Prayagraj, Meerut and Agra. Seven Software Technology Parks are operational in the state, while new IT parks are being developed in Varanasi, Bareilly, Kanpur and Gorakhpur, he said. He said Noida and Lucknow were being developed as deep-tech hubs under the new startup policy and work was progressing on developing an AI city and a broader AI ecosystem in Lucknow. The CM also highlighted HCL's social initiatives in Uttar Pradesh, saying its programmes had reached more than 50 lakh people and over 3,000 villages during the past 10-11 years. He said HCL had contributed to education, rural livelihoods and community development through its initiatives in districts including Sitapur and Bulandshahr. "Development does not mean merely building large campuses in big cities. Real development is when a farmer in a village gets access to better technology, women get new livelihood opportunities, children get better education and healthcare, and rural youth become part of the new economy," Adityanath said. HCLTech Chairperson Roshni Nadar Malhotra said Uttar Pradesh was the "karmabhoomi" and home of the HCL Group and that the company had an "unwavering belief" in the state's talent and opportunities.

title: Tablet shipments decline 3.8 pc YoY, hit by memory price inflation: Report
content: New Delhi, Oct 6 (PTI) Tablet PC shipments in India declined by 3.8 per cent year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026 due to a rise in memory chip prices, market research firm Counterpoint Research said on Tuesday. The tablet PC segment priced below ₹ 20,000 was most impacted by the memory price hike, with a 43 per cent dip in supplies during the reported quarter. "Tablet shipments in India declined 3.8 per cent YoY in Q2 2026. The decline was driven by brands starting to pass higher input costs on to consumers, increasing overall selling prices. India's tablet market has begun to face pressure from memory price inflation, more prominently from Q2 2026 onwards," the research firm said. Counterpoint Research said that the brands have increased prices across their portfolios and streamlined memory variants. "The sub- ₹ 20,000 segment, which has traditionally formed the backbone of India's tablet market, was most impacted by the memory price hike, declining 43 per cent YoY in Q2. The above ₹ 20,000 segment emerged as a key battleground, growing 27 per cent and capturing 74 per cent of the market. This was driven by brands increasing prices and streamlining their portfolios, with consumers moving towards premium products," Counterpoint Research Principal Analyst Anshika Jain said. According to the firm, the shift towards the higher-price segment resulted in a 15 per cent increase in average selling price, she said. "There has been a notable movement in the market towards larger screen sizes, especially for screens larger than 12 inches, at a price point greater than ₹ 20,000, as consumers increasingly view the tablets as a secondary screen," Jain said. The ₹ 20,000 to ₹ 30,000 price band saw strong growth of 45 per cent YoY, supported by brands such as OnePlus and Lenovo. Despite a dip in supplies, domestic manufacturing grew 30 per cent YoY in Q2, as established players, such as Samsung and Lenovo, continued to expand their local production. "Brands including OnePlus and OPPO are also deepening their manufacturing presence in India. On the demand side, the impact of elevated memory prices is expected to continue in festive seasons, though the promotions might provide some support to demand," Jain said.

title: Frances Mistral announces new AI model
content: By Elizabeth Howcroft and Leo Marchandon PARIS, Oct 6 (Reuters) - French AI company Mistral on Tuesday announced a new AI model, which the company said outperforms some Chinese open-weight models. The 3-year-old startup is seen as Europe's best hope of fielding a home-grown competitor to US and lower-cost Chinese rivals. Mistral had not released a new model since May, and in August started making third-party models available to its customers, starting with Beijing-based Z.ai's GLM 5.3. Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch told a conference in Abu Dhabi that the new product beat Chinese models on some aspects, "including cyber", without giving details. Pierre Stock, Mistral's vice president of science, told Reuters that it ranked among the best open-weight options. Mistral said Le Chonk - officially named Mistral Large 4 - will be made fully public on October 27. In a preview period, some cybersecurity experts and state authorities will have access to a version with fewer safety barriers to test its capabilities, Mistral said. SAFETY FEARS Stock told Reuters the new model had tried to go beyond its testing environment, but attempts had been contained using software. OpenAI and Anthropic, whose models escaped their testing environments, have restricted access to their most cyber-capable systems. Mistral will release its model open-weight, meaning anyone can download and run it on their own servers. When US executives last month said AI could pose an existential threat to humanity, Mensch said the incumbents' comments were self-serving. Mistral, which raised €3 billion in its latest funding round, positions itself as a safer, European alternative. DESIGNING CHIPS Mistral said Large 4 is "closing the gap with frontier models" on coding, finance, geospatial analysis, manufacturing and product design. Mistral has trained the model on its own infrastructure. Stock said its goal is to partner "very deeply" with backers including ASML and new-investor Samsung "across the entire value chain". Stock said that Large 4 is capable of designing computer chips, but declined to comment on whether Mistral is currently developing chips with Samsung. (Reporting by Elizabeth Howcroft in Paris and Leo Marchandon in Gdansk. Additional reporting by Federico Maccioni in Abu Dhabi. Editing by Louise Heavens)

title: Poco X8 Power review: Great battery life and striking design, but does it justify ₹35,999 price tag?
content: POCO has recently launched the X8 Power in India, marking the company’s first smartphone in the country to cross the massive 10,000mAh battery threshold. The phone is priced at ₹ 35,999 and is designed for people looking for long battery life but don't wish to switch to a rugged or oversized phone. The X8 Power is also equipped with a 6.83-inch AMOLED screen, a Snapdragon 6 Gen 5 processor and a 50MP camera with IP69K waterproofing. The big question is whether the massive battery is enough to make the X8 Power stand out in the crowded mid-range segment. For users, particularly those with long workdays or lots of travelling, the answer is mostly yes. The mobile phone can extend beyond a day and, on moderate use, has a two-day battery life. However, its cameras and performance leave some room for improvement. View full Image Poco X8 Power box content. ( Pragya Singha Roy ) Battery The biggest attraction is obvious. The X8 Power sports a 10,000 mAh battery, eliminating most of the battery worries. I discovered that the handset was able to hold approximately 40-45% of its battery charge after an average workday. With moderate use, it lasted about two days. It might be possible to extend it to three days for lighter users. View full Image Poco X8 Power battery test. The phone scored 26 hours and 44 minutes in the PCMark battery test. It is also capable of 100W charging, but charging such a large battery is not necessarily fast. During testing, a full charge of the battery can be done in approximately 30-50 minutes. There is also 27W reverse charging. That makes the X8 Power a handy power source for another phone in an emergency. Also Read | CMF Watch 3 Pro review: Can its heart rate tracking keep up with daily fitness? Design Poco has taken a different design pattern for the X8 Power. The yellow variant gets a vegan leather back, a contrasting black frame and a camera module. It looks more unique than standard mid-range phones made up of glass and metal . View full Image Poco X8 Power. ( Pragya Singha Roy ) At 8.65 mm thick and 223 grams, the X8 Power is not light. This is partially due to the large battery. However, it's not so heavy that it feels excessively bulky, especially for a phone that has such a large battery. It is also dust and water-resistant with an IP69K rating. This is an extra security feature for people who spend a lot of time outside. Display The X8 Power is equipped with a 6.83-inch 120Hz refresh 1.5K AMOLED screen. The bezels are thin and uniform, and the Gorilla Glass Victus 2 is protected. Poco is claiming up to 3,500 nits of peak brightness. The outdoor visibility was good, as were the punchy colours, making it well-suited for video streaming. The panel is capable of displaying the entire DCI-P3 colour gamut, HDR performance on Netflix and HDR on YouTube. There are stereo speakers with Dolby Atmos for enhanced entertainment. Performance Qualcomm's Snapdragon 6 Gen 5 chipset is used in the X8 Power. The POCO X8 Power is the first smartphone in India to feature this new processor. Performance is quite good for normal use. Apps launch in a timely fashion, and application switching is usually easy. However, occasional stutters can appear during heavier multitasking. View full Image Poco X8 Power. This isn't a performance-first smartphone, though you can still play games. The game is able to support a max of 90 fps but can drop to lower frame rates during extended gameplay. Geekbench 7 scored 915 points in single-core and 2,851 points in multi-core tests. The variants have an important storage difference. The 256GB version receives faster UFS 4.1 storage, in addition to LPDDR5X RAM. The 128GB variant's storage is based on UFS 2.2. Cameras View full Image Poco X8 Power wide shot. View full Image Poco X8 Power. View full Image .. View full Image .. View full Image Poco has given the X8 Power a 50MP Sony IMX882 primary camera and an 8MP ultrawide camera. Poco has given the X8 Power a 50MP Sony IMX882 primary camera and an 8MP ultrawide camera. Selfies are taken with a 16MP camera. Good light performance with the main camera. Colouring is fairly reliable , but may be over-coloured at times. Portrait shots also include some smoothing of the skin. The ultrawide camera is adequate for occasional use but is not a major strength of the phone. Video recording is more impressive on paper. The rear camera is able to shoot 4K video at 30 frames per second (fps) and is equipped with optical image stabilisation. The selfie camera also has 4K at 30 fps, and the ultrawide camera is capped at 1080p at 30 fps. View full Image . ( Pragya Singha Roy ) HyperOS features The X8 Power is powered by HyperOS 3 running on Android 16. Users who have used Xiaomi or Poco phones will find the user interface familiar, as there are a few options to customise the launcher and lock screen. There is some pre-installed software, although most of it can be removed. The Indus Appstore is a system app and cannot be uninstalled. By default, Glance is turned off. Poco has guaranteed four years of OS updates and six years of security updates. This means the X8 Power has a longer software runway than other phones in the segment. Verdict: Battery first, everything else second The Poco X8 Power is an unusual phone because its biggest selling point changes the way you use it. A 10,000 mAh battery makes checking the battery percentage less significant. The display, durability and design are a plus, and the cameras and Snapdragon 6 Gen 5 chipset are sufficient for the average user. However, those seeking the primary purpose of gaming or camera features could pursue better options. The X8 Power is the clear choice for those who travel frequently, heavy chargers and those who just don't want to carry a charger around. The 256GB model, at ₹ 38,999, is the more sensible choice, especially as it upgrades the storage from UFS 2.2 to UFS 4.1. Also Read | iPhone Duo yield near 60%: Why Apple's foldable faces supply woes In short, the Poco X8 Power is not trying to be the fastest camera phone or the strongest gaming device in its price range. It is doing something simpler: making battery anxiety almost irrelevant. I rate the Poco X8 Power 7.3/10.

title: Can Temple check if pilots are fit to fly? Deepinder Goyal suggests Air Force could use it too
content: Deepinder Goyal ’s Temple wearable is expected to roll out soon in India. Ahead of opening its pre-orders, Goyal claimed that Temple will be able to check the fitness of pilots before flights. His revelation came days after the FlyDubai incident, where a co-pilot attacked Captain Smit Machchhar during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv in an alleged attempt to crash the flight carrying more than 170 passengers. Temple can be used by pilots and air force Taking to X, Deepinder Goyal said that Temple can also be used by the air force authorities. He said that the wearable would be able to determine the fitness of pilots before taking on a mission. After Goyal announced that Temple would be available in six different colour options, someone wrote to him on X, “One interesting use case for @temple could be giving it to restaurant managers & head chefs. It would be fun to see the data on a dry day vs weekend vs weekday. Would be even more interesting to see shifts till around 7pm and then from 7pm to say 1am. Can this be eventually hooked to an API and detect if a chef is going thru stressful time, cause the supply chain is running late and they risk shortage of raw-materials? I gotta get my hands on this soon (sic).” Responding to the suggestion, Goyal revealed, “I would certainly have it on pilots to check if they are fit to fly. And on the air force to check who is the fittest to fly a mission today.” What is Temple? Temple is a wearable designed to sit on the side of the head, somewhere near the temple area, between the forehead and ear. Unlike other wearables such as smartwatches, Temple is intended to collect information linked to blood flow to the brain. The technology behind it is called BrainFlow. Also Read | Deepinder Goyal reveals six colours for Temple ahead of pre-orders Deepinder Goyal reveals ahead of launch The Zomato founder previously said that Temple will be able to read people's intent. He said that currently research is underway on a thoughts-to-text tech. However, he said that such development would take a few more years. It is expected to be available in the third or fourth version of Temple. Also Read | Does Temple 'stick to your skin'? Can you bathe with it? Deepinder Goyal answers Talking about Temple, Goyal also briefly commented on whether Temple would come with any age restrictions. “We use a PPG sensor. Same as Apple Watch, and other wearables. Nothing in there which can hurt a developing brain. Having said that, I don’t see why anybody less than 18 years would need a Temple, unless they are aiming to go to the Olympics,” he said.

title: Flipkart Big Billion Days 2026: Are 1.0,000mAh batteries the new smartphone must-have?
content: Flipkart Big Billion Days 2026 is set to begin on October 8, bringing discounts, bank offers and No Cost EMI deals on smartphones across price segments. The vivo T5 Lite 5G has a 6,500mAh battery, 44W charging and a 120Hz display. It is priced at ₹ 22,999. Motorola's Moto G77 Power also packs a 7,000 mAh battery. Nothing takes a different approach Nothing also offers benefits during Flipkart Big Billion Days 2026, but its smartphones show that a bigger battery is not the only way to compete. It has a 5,400 mAh battery, a Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 processor and a 6.78‑inch 1.5K 120 Hz AMOLED display. The Nothing Phone (4a) Pro offers a ₹ 4,500 bank offer and a ₹ 500 exchange bonus. The price begins at ₹ 49,999 for the 8GB+128GB version. It has a 6.83‑inch 1.5K 144Hz AMOLED display and a Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 processor. Processor efficiency, display technology, refresh rate, software optimisation and charging speed also shape a phone’s endurance. During Flipkart Big Billion Days 2026, customers will have a variety of options. Those who prioritise maximum endurance can look at the realme P4 Power 5G, POCO X8 Power, POCO X8 Pro Max or POCO X8, while buyers seeking a more balanced package can consider the realme P4x 5G, realme P4 Lite 5G, vivo T5x, vivo T5, Moto G77 Power, Nothing Phone (4a), Nothing Phone (4a) Pro or Nothing Phone (4b). With the sale starting on October 8, 2026, the biggest change may be that a 7,000 mAh-plus battery is no longer unusual. This battery size is quickly turning into a selling point for brands that want to attract smartphone buyers.

title: Your student ID can get you free Gemini AI, Photoshop and more: How to claim
content: A college ID can be more valuable than just proof of enrolment. Students in India can use their student status to access discounted or free services across categories such as artificial intelligence, entertainment, travel, software and electronics. Several companies offer special plans and deals for students. Google, Spotify, Apple, IndiGo, Adobe, Samsung and GitHub are among the companies with student benefits. Eligibility criteria, verification requirements and offer periods can vary, so students should check the terms before signing up. Free Gemini AI and 400GB storage Google is currently offering university students aged 18 and above a free one-year subscription to Google AI Plus. The offer includes Gemini usage limits, 400GB of cloud storage and access to Gemini Omni . Students also get unlimited uploads for features such as Study Notebooks, Visuals and Live. Google announced the student offer on August 19, 2026. According to the company, students can claim the offer until December 31, 2026. After the free period ends, the plan costs ₹ 399 per month unless cancelled. Also Read | CMF Watch 3 Pro review: Can its heart rate tracking keep up with daily fitness? Spotify and Apple Music at ₹ 69 per month Entertainment subscriptions are also more affordable for students who are eligible. Spotify Premium Student in India costs ₹ 69 each month after the offer, and the student status is checked through SheerID. Apple Music also has a student plan that costs ₹ 69 each month. Apple Music includes Apple TV access with the plan. Students can keep the student price for up to four years as long as they are still eligible. YouTube also has a student membership in India. However, the ₹ 89 monthly price mentioned on some websites should not be treated as a confirmed current rate. YouTube requires students to study at an eligible institution and verify their status through SheerID. Student fares can mean cheaper flights IndiGo's Student Fare can give you up to 10% off the base price of domestic flights plus an extra 10 kg of baggage space depending on the airline's rules and availability. Students can use a real student ID or an acceptance letter to check, according to the IndiGo press release from November 22, 2024. Here’s what we know Apple and Samsung offer discounts on gadgets Apple's Education Store gives prices on eligible Macs and iPads. Apple's India education store currently shows the MacBook Air starting at ₹ 137,900 with education discounts. Samsung has its Student Advantage programme. According to Samsung, students at select institutes can get up to 10% off on eligible Galaxy products, but the actual discount depends on the product and the school. GitHub benefits for student developers Students who like coding can apply for the GitHub Student Developer Pack. GitHub says the program includes GitHub Copilot Student and other partner benefits, which can include some domains and cloud credits.
